ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the parabola $y=x^{2}+5x+4$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $A$ (point $A$ is to the left of the axis of symmetry of this parabola), and intersects the $y$-axis at point $B$. The line segment $AB$ intersects the axis of symmetry of the parabola at point $P$. $OA=OB$. Find the coordinates of point $P$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \text{ Let the equation of line AB be } y=kx+b, \]
\[ \text{then } \begin{cases} b=4 \\ 4k+b=0 \end{cases} \]
\[ \text{Solving yields } \begin{cases} k=-1 \\ b=4 \end{cases} \]
\[ \therefore \text{ the equation of line AB is } y=-x+4, \]
\[ \because \text{ the axis of symmetry of the parabola is the line } x=-\frac{5}{2}, \]
\[ \therefore \text{ when } x=-\frac{5}{2}, y=-\frac{5}{2}+4=\frac{3}{2}, \]
\[ \therefore \text{ the coordinates of point } P \text{ are } \boxed{\left(-\frac{5}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)}. \]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: In the coordinate system in the figure there is a parabola opening upward, point A is located on the negative half-axis of the x-axis, point B is located on the positive half-axis of the y-axis, line segment AB slopes from the lower left to the upper right, and intersects the vertical axis of symmetry of the parabola at point P. In the figure P is above the x-axis, and is located between A and B. Then reason: The parabola is y=x^2+5x+4, which can be factorized as y=(x+1)(x+4). Therefore the abscissas of its two intersections with the x-axis are x=-1 and x=-4. The axis of symmetry of the parabola is x=-\frac{5}{2}; the problem states that A is on the left side of the axis of symmetry, so A=(-4,0). The parabola intersects the y-axis at point B; let x=0, get y=4, so B=(0,4). This is also consistent with OA=OB=4. Line AB passes through A(-4,0) and B(0,4), and the slope is k=\frac{4-0}{0-(-4)}=1, so the equation of line AB is y=x+4. Point P is the intersection point of line AB and the axis of symmetry x=-\frac{5}{2}. Substitute x=-\frac{5}{2} into y=x+4, get y=-\frac{5}{2}+4=\frac{3}{2}. Therefore the coordinates of P are \left(-\frac{5}{2},\frac{3}{2}\right).
